cases.sentence: В середине этого ___ Пьера позвали к главнокомандующему.
cases.explain: «нового рассказа» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: In the middle of this fresh tale Pierre was summoned to the commander in chief.

cases.sentence: ___ говорил что-то и, как только вошел Пьер, замолчал и вышел.
cases.explain: «Невысокий человек» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: When he entered the private room Count Rostopchín, puckering his face, was rubbing his forehead and eyes with his hand. A short man was saying something, but when Pierre entered he stopped speaking and went out.

cases.sentence: — сказал граф Растопчин ___, как будто было что-то дурное в этом, но что он намерен был простить.
cases.explain: «строгим тоном» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Ah, how do you do, great warrior?” said Rostopchín as soon as the short man had left the room. “We have heard of your prowess. But that’s not the point. Between ourselves, mon cher, do you belong to the Masons?” he went on severely, as though there were something wrong about it which he nevertheless intended to pardon. Pierre remained silent. “I am well informed, my friend, but I am aware that there are Masons and I hope that you are not one of those who on pretense of saving mankind wish to ruin Russia.”

cases.sentence: Вы можете понимать, что на это есть причины и что я не мог бы сослать здешнего почт-директора, ежели бы он не был ___.
cases.explain: «вредный человек» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “There, you see, mon cher! I expect you know that Messrs. Speránski and Magnítski have been deported to their proper place. Mr. Klyucharëv has been treated in the same way, and so have others who on the plea of building up the temple of Solomon have tried to destroy the temple of their fatherland. You can understand that there are reasons for this and that I could not have exiled the Postmaster had he not been a harmful person. It has now come to my knowledge that you lent him your carriage for his removal from town, and that you have even accepted papers from him for safe custody. I like you and don’t wish you any harm and—as you are only half my age—I advise you, as a father would, to cease all communication with men of that stamp and to leave here as soon as possible.”

cases.sentence: — Eh bien, mon cher, qu’est ce que vous faites, vous personnellement?[764] Мы накануне ___, и мне некогда быть любезным со всеми, с кем у меня есть дело.
cases.explain: «общего бедствия» — after the preposition «накануне», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “There we are!” Rostopchín shouted at Pierre louder than before, frowning suddenly. “Vereshchágin is a renegade and a traitor who will be punished as he deserves,” said he with the vindictive heat with which people speak when recalling an insult. “But I did not summon you to discuss my actions, but to give you advice—or an order if you prefer it. I beg you to leave the town and break off all communication with such men as Klyucharëv. And I will knock the nonsense out of anybody”—but probably realizing that he was shouting at Bezúkhov who so far was not guilty of anything, he added, taking Pierre’s hand in a friendly manner, “We are on the eve of a public disaster and I haven’t time to be polite to everybody who has business with me. My head is sometimes in a whirl. Well, mon cher, what are you doing personally?”

cases.sentence: — Mais rien,[765] Да ничего, — отвечал Пьер, все не поднимая глаз и не изменяя выражения ___.
cases.explain: «задумчивого лица» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Why, nothing,” answered Pierre without raising his eyes or changing the thoughtful expression of his face.

cases.sentence: — Un conseil d’ami, mon cher. Décampez et au plutôt, c’est tout ce que je vous dis. A bon entendeur salut![766] ___.
cases.explain: «Дружеский совет» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “A word of friendly advice, mon cher. Be off as soon as you can, that’s all I have to tell you. Happy he who has ears to hear. Goodbye, my dear fellow. Oh, by the by!” he shouted through the doorway after Pierre, “is it true that the countess has fallen into the clutches of the holy fathers of the Society of Jesus?”

cases.sentence: Ах, да, — прокричал он ему из двери, — правда ли, что графиня попалась в лапки des saints pères de la Société de Jésus?[767] ___ Общества Иисусова?
cases.explain: «святых отцов» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “A word of friendly advice, mon cher. Be off as soon as you can, that’s all I have to tell you. Happy he who has ears to hear. Goodbye, my dear fellow. Oh, by the by!” he shouted through the doorway after Pierre, “is it true that the countess has fallen into the clutches of the holy fathers of the Society of Jesus?”

cases.sentence: Человек восемь ___ побывало у него в этот вечер.
cases.explain: «разных людей» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: When he reached home it was already getting dark. Some eight people had come to see him that evening: the secretary of a committee, the colonel of his battalion, his steward, his majordomo, and various petitioners. They all had business with Pierre and wanted decisions from him. Pierre did not understand and was not interested in any of these questions and only answered them in order to get rid of these people. When left alone at last he opened and read his wife’s letter.

cases.sentence: Секретарь комитета, полковник его батальона, управляющий, дворецкий и ___.
cases.explain: «разные просители» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: When he reached home it was already getting dark. Some eight people had come to see him that evening: the secretary of a committee, the colonel of his battalion, his steward, his majordomo, and various petitioners. They all had business with Pierre and wanted decisions from him. Pierre did not understand and was not interested in any of these questions and only answered them in order to get rid of these people. When left alone at last he opened and read his wife’s letter.

cases.sentence: Когда он проснулся на другой день утром, дворецкий пришел доложить, что от графа Растопчина пришел нарочно посланный ___ — узнать, уехал ли или уезжает ли граф Безухов.
cases.explain: «полицейский чиновник» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: When he awoke next morning the majordomo came to inform him that a special messenger, a police officer, had come from Count Rostopchín to know whether Count Bezúkhov had left or was leaving the town.

cases.sentence: Человек десять ___, имеющих дело до Пьера, ждали его в гостиной.
cases.explain: «разных людей» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: A dozen persons who had business with Pierre were awaiting him in the drawing room. Pierre dressed hurriedly and, instead of going to see them, went to the back porch and out through the gate.

cases.sentence: С тех пор и до конца ___, никто из домашних Безуховых, несмотря на все поиски, не видал больше Пьера и не знал, где он находился.
cases.explain: «московского разорения» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: From that time till the end of the destruction of Moscow no one of Bezúkhov’s household, despite all the search they made, saw Pierre again or knew where he was.
